news.Title: MCHP Rides on Open-Standard Connectivity: Can It Beat ADI & TXN?
news.Content:
Microchip Technology MCHP is strengthening its automotive connectivity portfolio through an open-standard display connectivity solution aimed at software-defined vehicles. Based on ASA Motion Link (ASA-ML) technology, the offering is designed to stream high-speed graphics and video from centralized vehicle computers to automotive displays while improving interoperability and reducing reliance on proprietary architectures. The solution is expected to expand MCHP's opportunity across automotive infotainment, advanced driver-assistance systems (ADAS), digital cockpits and human-machine interfaces, improving competitive positioning against Texas Instruments TXN and Analog Devices ADI.

The opportunity comes as Microchip Technologies' automotive business gains momentum. In the first quarter of fiscal 2027, automotive accounted for an estimated 15% of MCHP's revenues, while sales from the automotive end market increased 29.3% year over year. The company indicated that the automotive market remains in the early stages of recovery, leaving room for further growth. Microchip already serves applications involving touch screens, graphical user interfaces, automotive safety, ADAS, networking and infotainment, making display connectivity a natural extension of its existing automotive footprint.

The open-standard push complements MCHP's broader Total System Solution strategy. The company's semiconductor portfolio spans microcontrollers, analog, interface, timing, security and wired-connectivity products. Microchip's specialized microcontrollers address automotive, human-machine interface, security and wired-connectivity applications, while the analog portfolio includes Ethernet and other interface products. This breadth could allow Microchip to compete for multiple sockets within a software-defined vehicle rather than depend solely on a stand-alone display-connectivity chip.

Microchip Technologies' broader capabilities could provide an additional competitive advantage. The company competes on performance, mixed-signal integration, low power consumption, reliability, security and functional safety. The company also highlights hardware-software compatibility, dependable delivery, time to market, total solution cost and easy-to-adopt reference designs as important competitive factors. These capabilities are relevant as automakers integrate displays, networking, control and security functions into increasingly centralized vehicle architectures. An anchor connectivity design win could therefore create opportunities for complementary analog, security and control products, potentially increasing Microchip's semiconductor content per vehicle.

Story Continues

MCHP Faces Tough Competition

Texas Instruments presents a strong competitive benchmark, supported by its broad Analog and Embedded Processing portfolios, accelerating automotive demand and strong capacity position. TXN's automotive revenues increased in the mid-teens year over year and upper single digits sequentially in the second quarter of 2026. TXN also said capacity and inventory investments are helping it respond to accelerating customer demand. Management has highlighted significant generation-over-generation content growth and opportunities to gain share as customers adopt new systems. Competitive lead times and available capacity could also help TXN win new designs when competitors face supply constraints.

Analog Devices represents another formidable challenge, particularly given its strength in automotive applications such as ADAS and infotainment. Automotive accounted for 25% of ADI's third-quarter fiscal 2026 revenues, with sales rising 16% year over year and 14% sequentially. The company linked the growth to higher content and share positions, with strength across next-generation ADAS, infotainment systems and electric powertrains. ADI sees autonomous mobility as part of the second generation of AI, where real-time sensing, inference and responsiveness become increasingly important. The company's higher automotive content and share positions could make it harder for MCHP to capture display-connectivity design wins, despite the appeal of Microchip's open-standard approach.

news.Title: LITE's Laser Growth Accelerates: Can It Challenge AVGO & AAOI?
news.Content:
Lumentum LITE is benefiting from accelerating demand for pump, electro-absorption modulated laser (EML) and continuous-wave (CW) lasers as hyperscalers expand artificial intelligence (AI) training, inference and data-center interconnect infrastructure. Rising bandwidth requirements are accelerating the transition toward 800G, 1.6T, near-packaged optics (NPO) and co-packaged optics (CPO). This trend strengthens Lumentum's position in high-speed optical connectivity and strengthens its competitive prowess against Broadcom AVGO and Applied Optoelectronics AAOI as AI clusters require increasingly dense optical links.

Pump lasers are emerging as a key growth driver. Lumentum's pump laser shipments increased more than 80% year over year in the fourth quarter of fiscal 2026, while demand continues to exceed available supply despite capacity expansion. AI training and inference are increasing full-rate connectivity requirements between data centers, driving scale-across deployments. The company expects pump laser shipments to increase roughly fourfold over the next several quarters and has secured multiple long-term customer agreements that help offset planned capital expenditures required to expand production.

Demand for Lumentum's EML portfolio is strengthening as customers migrate toward higher lane speeds. In the fourth quarter of fiscal 2026, 200G-per-lane EMLs represented more than 25% of total EML revenues. The company expects 200G EMLs to account for 50% or more of shipment volumes by mid-2027. LITE is expanding capacity across its two indium-phosphide fabs in Japan for upcoming 200G and 300G-per-lane opportunities and remains on track for more than 50% year-over-year EML unit growth in the third quarter of fiscal 2027.

CW and ultra-high-power lasers provide additional growth opportunities. Lumentum's tight laser specifications are helping customers improve transceiver manufacturing yields, supporting premium pricing. The company has narrowed the margin gap between its CW and EML products. Ultra-high-power laser revenues are expected to approach $50 million by the end of calendar 2026, with the business potentially reaching its first triple-digit quarterly revenue level in the third quarter of fiscal 2027. Meanwhile, LITE's 120-milliwatt, 150-milliwatt and 400-milliwatt laser technologies position it to benefit as NPO and CPO increasingly move optics closer to AI accelerators.

LITE Faces Tough Competition

Broadcom competes directly with Lumentum across high-speed optical connectivity. AVGO's portfolio spans CPO, 1.6T DSPs, CW and EML lasers, alongside 200G and 400G SerDes, Ethernet switches and fabric solutions. The company also has substantial scale in AI infrastructure, with AI semiconductor revenues surging 221% year over year to $16.7 billion in the third quarter of fiscal 2026. AI networking revenues increased more than 2.5 times year over year during the quarter. Its integrated portfolio of switches, DSPs, lasers, NICs and routers, combined with strong hyperscaler relationships, could help Broadcom capture a greater share of optical content as AI clusters expand.

Applied Optoelectronics is strengthening its position primarily in high-power and CPO lasers. AAOI is expanding in-house laser and external light source (ELSFP) production, with ELSFP capacity targeted to reach roughly 400,000 units per month in 2028. Its existing laser-fab capacity is expected to increase almost 300% by the third quarter of 2027, while a second Houston-area fab is planned at roughly four times the size of its current facility. AAOI is working with at least five CPO customers. These investments could intensify competition for Lumentum as demand for high-power optical sources and next-generation AI connectivity continues to rise.

news.Title: AXT's Liquidity Supports InP Capacity Expansion: Can Growth Continue?
news.Content:
AXT, Inc. AXTI has the financial strength to support aggressive indium phosphide (InP) capacity expansion, positioning the company to capitalize on strong AI data-center demand.

AXT ended the second quarter with $748.8 million in cash, cash equivalents and investments, up $625.6 million sequentially, primarily following its April secondary offering, which generated approximately $632 million before expenses. This strengthened liquidity provides financial flexibility to expand its manufacturing footprint.

The timing is favorable because InP demand continues to exceed supply. AXT has committed to doubling InP capacity in 2026 and is ahead of schedule while planning another expansion in 2027. Its InP backlog has surpassed $100 million, providing visibility into future demand.

Customer commitments further strengthen the outlook. Long-term agreements with Casela and Coherent include wafer commitments and prepayments, while AXT's Lumentum agreement reserves InP capacity through 2031.

Importantly, AXT's second-quarter revenues reached a record $47.6 million, while GAAP gross margin climbed to 44.9%. The Zacks Consensus Estimate projects 2026 and 2027 revenue growth of 146.4% and 108.4%, respectively. Thus, strong liquidity and planned InP expansion provide a solid foundation for continued growth.

InP Capacity Race Raises Competitive Pressure on AXT

Coherent COHR is challenging AXTI by rapidly expanding its own InP production. COHR plans to double internal InP output year over year and more than double it again by the end of 2027. As COHR increases 6-inch production for EMLs, CW lasers and photodiodes, COHR's vertical integration could reduce reliance on suppliers such as AXTI, intensifying competition.

Lumentum LITE is expanding internal InP wafer capacity across two Japanese fabs while converting its Greensboro facility from gallium arsenide to InP. The company also secured additional substrate supply from AXTI because demand surged. Lumentum is both a customer and a competitor of AXTI. As LITE ramps up its own InP production, it may need to source fewer products from AXTI.

news.Title: Analog Devices Shows Why AI Is Not the Only Story Driving Chip Demand
news.Content:
Key Points

Interested in Analog Devices, Inc.? Here are five stocks we like better.

Analog Devices delivered a record fiscal third quarter, with data center strength leading growth, while industrial and automotive also contributed meaningfully.

Industrial revenue accounted for nearly half of Analog's quarterly sales, indicating that the semiconductor recovery is broader than AI infrastructure alone.

Microchip Technology offers a similar diversified chip setup, with exposure to industrial, automotive, aerospace, defense and data center markets.

It seems all but confirmed that 2026 will be a year given over to AI, with chipmakers like NVIDIA Corp. (NASDAQ: NVDA) always at the forefront of discussions of the potential for further growth. Companies tied to data center infrastructure buildout have thrived as industries pour billions of dollars into creating more AI computing capacity.

At least one global semiconductor firm is showing a different path that has also yielded strong results, however. Analog Devices (NASDAQ: ADI) has undoubtedly benefited from the AI-related surge, as shares are up by 33% year to date (YTD).

→ 3 Under-the-Radar Defense Stocks With Record Backlogs

However, the company's latest quarter results demonstrate that there are other growth areas as well. Namely, industrial and automotive markets show strong potential to drive chipmakers like Analog in the coming quarters, even as these industries are often overshadowed by the focus on AI.

A Closer Look at Analog's Latest Earnings

For fiscal Q3 2026 ending Aug. 1, Analog reported strong results that investors might easily attribute to its connection with the rapidly expanding AI sector. Analog's 39% year-over-year (YOY) revenue gains, for example, led to more than $4 billion in revenue for the quarter, more than $100 million above analyst estimates. Earnings per share (EPS) also climbed substantially and beat analyst expectations.

→ Ride-Share Reckoning: Tesla Drives Into Uber's Lane

To be sure, these guidance-beating metrics were due in large part to the company's data center business, which saw revenue more than double YOY in both the optical and power categories. The company's addressable market in the data center space is also growing quickly, a sign that management's expectation of double-digit growth in these markets over the next three or more years may be reasonable.

What Can Industrial and Automotive Applications Mean for Analog?

What these headlines potentially obscure, however, is that Analog's recovery as a semiconductor company is more broad than just the AI industry. Indeed, Analog's latest results would suggest that demand for semiconductor products is returning across a more traditional slice of the economy. Industrial revenue, for instance, made up 49% of the company's total sales last quarter, reaching just under $2 billion after surging by 53% YOY. This was due to automation, electronic test and measurement, aerospace and defense, and other demand.

Story Continues

→ Petco Is Still Being Priced Like the Old Petco

Industrial applications are largely independent of AI, so these growth factors could continue to contribute to Analog's top-line gains even if AI infrastructure spending slows. This may help to make the company's performance more durable over the longer term.

Automotive is also a corner of the market that could benefit Analog in the quarters to come. Revenue from the automotive category climbed 16% YOY last quarter and represented about a quarter of the company's sales for that period. As more driver-assistance and infotainment systems require next-generation semiconductor hardware, Analog is demonstrating that it can meet this need.

Both industrial and automotive business have been major drivers of Analog's sales up to this point, and secular trends might suggest that these industries will continue to fuel sales growth for the foreseeable future.

What Broad Semiconductor Demand Means for Analog and Its Competitors

As semiconductor demand grows across industries, a company like Analog may become increasingly stable. The company's chips help connect the digital and physical worlds through functions such as sensing, power management, signal conversion, and more. This makes them vital for a host of applications ranging from automation to medical tools to aerospace. In turn, Analog's business may be more durable than those chipmakers that have increasingly become dedicated to a single industry, such as AI, in case demand in one part of the market collapses.

Analog is not the only company in a position to benefit here. Microchip Technology Inc. (NASDAQ: MCHP) is another diversified semiconductor maker with products that are valuable for automotive, industrial, aerospace, and other applications. It also had strong recent results pointing to a broader semiconductor recovery not exclusively reliant on AI.

Perhaps the clearest signal for investors that these companies could be poised to benefit from rising demand across industries is how Wall Street analysts view them. ADI shares, for instance, have a stellar 28 Buy ratings and just two Holds, plus a predicted 25% upside. MCHP stock is not far behind, with 16 Buy ratings and eight Holds, and it enjoys an even more promising 33% in anticipated upside. While neither company is risk-free, both are well positioned to thrive whether or not the AI boom continues.

news.Title: Sanmina vs. Silicon Motion: Which AI Stock Has More Upside Now?
news.Content:
Sanmina Corporation SANM and Silicon Motion Technology Corporation SIMO are key players in the broader technology hardware ecosystem with significant exposure to the AI and data-center infrastructure buildout. Sanmina is a key player in the electronics manufacturing services (EMS) industry. It focuses on engineering and fabricating complex components and on providing complete end-to-end supply chain solutions to original equipment manufacturers (OEMs) across various end markets.

Silicon Motion is a leading developer of microcontroller ICs for NAND flash storage devices. The semiconductor company also designs, develops and markets high-performance, low-power semiconductor solutions for OEMs and other customers.

Let us delve a little deeper into the companies' competitive dynamics to understand which of the two is relatively better placed in the industry.

The Case for Sanmina

Sanmina is increasingly focusing on 42Q connected manufacturing that effectively integrates data from customers' global factories and suppliers' fleets and creates an up-to-date information base. It offers a unified data ecosystem with real-time data analytics capabilities that significantly improve visibility across the enterprise's distributed manufacturing and accelerate the decision-making process. Sanmina has deployed the 42Q connected manufacturing in more than 70 factories across 15 countries, connecting more than 35,000 pieces of manufacturing equipment in the cloud. Such a technology-driven, customer-focused approach enables Sanmina to work closely with its customers to anticipate future manufacturing requirements and modify its R&D initiatives accordingly. Attracting and developing strong customer relationships by delivering high-level customer service is one of the key strategies to drive commercial expansion.

Sanmina has acquired the data center infrastructure manufacturing business from AMD to scale up production for cloud and AI hyperscale customers. It is positioning itself as an end-to-end manufacturing partner for AI data centers, spanning accelerated compute, AI racks, liquid cooling, networking, storage and power infrastructure. The company offers end-to-end solutions that include product design, manufacturing, assembly, testing and aftermarket support. Such an end-to-end approach allows clients to rely on a single partner throughout the product lifecycle management. Its vertically integrated manufacturing process brings several other advantages. This approach streamlines processes and lowers costs, enabling Sanmina to achieve greater economies of scale.

However, Sanmina has been heavily affected by supply-chain disruptions over the past few years. Owing to current geopolitical events, the company is currently experiencing delays and shortages of critical components, including capacitors, resistors and more. Management expects supply chain issues to persist in the short to medium term. Intensifying competition in the EMS industry has hurt Sanmina's net sales. The company faces stiff competition from larger players like Jabil, Inc. JBL. It generates about 80% of its net sales from products manufactured outside the United States, which exposes it to political and economic disruptions in the operating countries. The company also has major production facilities in China. The recent imposition of tariffs on these countries by the U.S. government has increased the cost of sales and strained margins.

Story Continues

The Case for SIMO

Silicon Motion has established itself as the leading merchant supplier of client SSD (solid-state drive) controllers to module makers, including most market leaders in the United States, Taiwan and China. The company believes that it is well-equipped to adapt to industry changes as it has collaborated with flash vendors to develop proprietary controller technology to overcome the existing weakness of 3D NAND and outshine peers. Silicon Motion has commenced initial sales of 3D SSD controllers to flash partners. It expects this controller to be a significant SSD controller growth driver for the next year, as NAND Flash partners' 3D capacity expands.

Silicon Motion operates a fabless business model, focusing on chip design while outsourcing manufacturing to foundries like TSMC. Consequently, the company has a low capital investment requirement as it does not require expensive fabrication plants, enabling it to adopt advanced manufacturing nodes quickly, leading to higher margins compared to integrated manufacturers. This, in turn, enables the company to focus on innovation and product development rather than manufacturing complexity. The key growth drivers for SIMO include AI and high-performance computing, cloud data centers, automotive storage, smartphones and mobile devices. Each of these end markets is growing fast and offers lucrative growth potential. Over the last 10 years, the company has shipped more than 5 billion controllers cumulatively – more than any other company in the world. Silicon Motion ships more than 750 million NAND controllers on average every year.

However, sluggishness in the global economy is likely to weigh on the company's wireless and broader semiconductor market. The demand for PCs and smartphones in the end market continues to be soft as numerous suppliers are focusing on reducing their inventory levels. The near-term price fluctuation in the PC market remains a concern. Silicon Motion continues to acquire a large number of companies. While this improves revenue opportunities, business mix and profitability, it also adds to integration risks. Moreover, the semiconductor industry is highly dynamic as it is prone to swift technological changes, stiff competition from evolving industry standards and declining average selling prices.

How Do Zacks Estimates Compare for SANM & SIMO?

The Zacks Consensus Estimate for Sanmina's fiscal 2026 sales implies year-over-year growth of 74.2%, while that of EPS suggests an improvement of 96.8%. The EPS estimates have moved up 6% over the past 60 days.

Image Source: Zacks Investment Research

The Zacks Consensus Estimate for Silicon Motion's 2026 sales indicates a year-over-year rise of 112.9%, while that for EPS suggests growth of 214.4%. The EPS estimates have trended up 24.6% over the past 60 days.

Price Performance & Valuation of SIMO & SANM

Over the past year, Silicon Motion has gained 224.1% compared with the industry's growth of 200.1%. Sanmina has surged 74.4% over the same period.

Silicon Motion looks more expensive than Sanmina from a valuation standpoint. Going by the price/sales ratio, SIMO's shares currently trade at 3.98 forward sales, higher than Sanmina's 0.68.

SANM or SIMO: Which is a Better Pick?

Both Silicon Motion and Sanmina sport a Zacks Rank #1 (Strong Buy). You can see the complete list of today's Zacks #1 Rank stocks here .

Both Silicon Motion and Sanmina expect sales and earnings to increase in the current fiscal year. In terms of price performance, SIMO has outperformed SANM. Silicon Motion has exhibited better estimate revisions than Sanmina, although it is trading relatively expensively in terms of valuation. Although there is not much to choose from, Silicon Motion seems to hold a slight competitive edge over Sanmina and is therefore a better investment option at the moment.

news.Title: ASE Technology Surges 16% in 3 Months: Time to Hold or Fold the Stock?
news.Content:
ASE Technology Holding ASX shares have rallied 15.9% in the past three months, outperforming the Zacks Electronics - Semiconductors industry's decline of 9.1%. The stock has also outperformed its industry peers, including United Microelectronics Corporation UMC, GlobalFoundries GFS and Synaptics SYNA. In the past three months, shares of United Microelectronics Corporation have returned 15.5%, while GlobalFoundries and Synaptics shares have plunged 39.7% and 26.5%, respectively.

The outperformance of ASE Technology's shares raises the question: Does it still have room to run, or is it time for investors to consider taking profits? Let's find out.

3-Month Price Return Performance

Image Source: Zacks Investment Research

Strong LEAP Momentum Boosts ASE Technology's Prospects

ASE Technology is seeing strong demand for its leading-edge advanced packaging (LEAP) services as the growth of AI increases demand for more complex semiconductor packaging and testing. LEAP revenues are tracking ahead of the company's earlier 2026 target of $3.5 billion. Management now expects to add another few hundred million dollars to this year's LEAP revenues and is targeting a doubling of LEAP revenues in 2027.

The company has clear visibility into customer demand and the capacity needed to support this growth. ASE plans to add facilities and equipment to expand LEAP capacity, with another $2 billion of CapEx added to its 2026 plans. Management said the company expects to continue making heavy investments in both advanced packaging and testing to support customer demand.

The growth is already showing up in ASE's results. In the second quarter of 2026, ATM revenues rose 36% year over year to TWD 126.1 billion. Higher LEAP volumes also helped lift ATM gross margin to 27.3% from 21.9% a year earlier. Management expects LEAP and test businesses to remain margin accretive and sees ATM gross margin moving above 30% in the fourth quarter of 2026.

Still, execution remains a key factor. ASE said its near-term growth is limited by how quickly it can install equipment and complete new facilities. ASE is working on 13 greenfield and eight brownfield projects. These projects are expected to provide capacity through 2028 and into part of 2029. However, managing so many projects at the same time might create execution risks, particularly around construction, equipment installation and meeting required timelines.

Nonetheless, strong AI-related demand, expanding capacity and higher-margin LEAP services give ASE a solid base for growth. Its target to double LEAP revenues in 2027 looks achievable, but timely capacity expansion and execution will be important for the company to meet that goal. The Zacks Consensus Estimate for 2026 and 2027 indicates revenue growth of around 27.9% and 22.5%, respectively.

Story Continues

Key Technical Indicator Signals Bullish Trend for ASX

ASX shares are trading above their 50-day & 200-day moving averages, a bullish technical signal that indicates the potential for continued upward momentum in the near term.

ASX 50-Day & 200-day Simple Moving Average

ASX's EMS Margins Remain Under Pressure

ASE Technology is seeing continued demand for its Electronics Manufacturing Services (EMS) business, but rising component costs and product mix are putting pressure on EMS profitability. This could remain a concern even as revenues grow.

In the second quarter of 2026, EMS revenues increased 6% sequentially to TWD 65.8 billion. However, EMS gross margin fell 0.6 percentage points sequentially to 8.9%, while EMS operating margin declined to 2.4% from 3.0% in the prior quarter. Management attributed the margin pressure to unfavorable product mix and a higher component cost environment. Further, EMS is also expected to lag the core ATM business in 2026. Management expects EMS revenue growth in 2026 to remain below 20% compared with more than 35% growth for ATM. This could limit EMS' contribution to ASE's overall growth.

The segment remains exposed to rising component prices. While management expects to pass higher costs through to customers, price increases can still pressure margins in the near term. For the third quarter of 2026, management expects the EMS operating margin to be around 3.2-3.4%, while noting that without component price increases, the margin would be closer to the typical seasonal level of 3.7-3.8%. This suggests that cost inflation remains a key factor behind the weaker profitability in the EMS business.

The above-mentioned factors show that continued component-cost inflation and unfavorable product mix could keep EMS margins low, limiting the benefit that ASE gets from revenue growth. This remains a key concern because the company is investing heavily across the business, while EMS remains a relatively lower-margin operation. Management acknowledged that higher memory/component costs can be passed through to customers, but the second quarter results show that this did not fully prevent near-term margin pressure. Overall, weak margins, higher component costs and slower growth than ATM remain key concerns for ASX's EMS business.

ASX's Premium Valuation Warrants a Cautious Approach

ASE Technology is currently trading at a higher price-to-earnings (P/E) multiple, significantly higher than the Zacks Electronics - Semiconductors industry. ASX's forward 12-month P/E ratio sits at 22.00X, significantly lower than the Zacks industry's trailing 12-month P/S ratio of 13.62X.

ASX stock also trades at a higher P/E multiple compared with other industry peers, including GlobalFoundries, United Microelectronics Corporation and Synaptics. At present, GlobalFoundries, United Microelectronics Corporation and Synaptics have P/E multiples of 18.78X, 18.21X and 17.66X, respectively.

ASX Forward 12-Month P/E Ratio

Conclusion: Hold ASX Stock Right Now

ASE Technology continues to benefit from strong demand for LEAP services as AI drives demand for advanced packaging and testing. Management expects LEAP revenues to grow further in 2026 and is targeting a doubling of LEAP revenues in 2027. Higher LEAP volumes are also helping improve ATM margins, while the company is adding capacity to support customer demand.

However, ASX's EMS business is seeing weaker margins due to higher component costs and an unfavorable product mix. Management expects EMS growth to remain below that of the ATM business in 2026, which could limit its contribution to overall growth. Further, the company's premium valuation warrants a cautious approach to the stock.

Currently, ASE Technology carries a Zacks Rank #3 (Hold). You can see the complete list of today's Zacks #1 Rank (Strong Buy) stocks here.

news.Title: 群聯8月營收282.76億元  年增377％  雙創歷史新高
news.Content:
NAND控制晶片大廠群聯電子9日公布8月營運成果，受惠AI基礎建設、AI推論與企業級儲存需求爆發，8月合併營收達新台幣282.76億元，月增4％、年增377％，刷新單月歷史新高；累計今年前8個月合併營收達1642.93億元，年增279％，同步改寫歷年同期新猷，單月與累計數據雙創歷史新高。

從出貨動能觀察，群聯8月控制晶片總出貨量較上月成長10％，其中高速PCIe SSD控制晶片出貨量月增幅更達77％，顯示AI伺服器與企業級儲存市場拉貨力道強勁。

群聯電子執行長潘健成指出，儲存市場需求持續反映在控制晶片出貨上，群聯正從傳統NAND控制晶片供應商，轉型為邊緣AI基礎建設與應用的賦能者；潘健成表示，群聯自主開發的Phison AI Data Platform已在台灣各產業加速落地，目前導入17家金融機構、30家醫療機構、18所大專院校、7個政府機關及超過70家中小企業，包括安泰銀行、新竹馬偕、陽明交大與苗栗縣政府等，成功驗證地端AI的實質應用需求。群聯內部亦建置11台AI伺服器，超過72％員工導入日常作業，實質帶動內部營運產出與效率提升。

展望後續營運，群聯表示，下一步將把在台灣累積的邊緣AI落地經驗複製至全球市場，特別是規模龐大的中小企業客群，後續將透過合資（Joint Venture）及策略合作模式拓展全球布局。隨著AI從大型資料中心走向各產業工作現場，群聯除了持續受惠儲存需求增溫，也將進一步放大AI整合方案的營收貢獻，奠定長期營運成長基礎。

news.Title: Teradyne Rides on Strong UltraFLEXplus Demand: Can It Beat KLAC & COHU?
news.Content:
Teradyne TER is benefiting from accelerating artificial intelligence (AI)-driven semiconductor test demand, particularly across high-performance compute, networking, and advanced memory applications, positioning the company as a formidable player against KLA KLAC and Cohu COHU. The company's growing demand for its UltraFLEXplus system, which is designed to address the complex testing requirements of high-performance processors and networking devices, has been noteworthy. UltraFLEXplus enables customers to reduce test development time, driving higher-efficiency volume production.

Building on this momentum, Teradyne recently launched three new instruments for its UltraFLEXplus semiconductor test platform to address growing AI and data-center computing requirements. The UltraPin5000-EM offers expanded vector memory and faster pattern loading for complex AI devices, while UltraPort-PCIe6 supports PCIe Gen6 testing at 64 Gbps across 32 lanes. The UltraVS64-HP delivers up to 1,280 amps per instrument to test increasingly power-intensive compute devices. Together, the products expand UltraFLEXplus capabilities across advanced digital, high-speed interface and power testing, supporting semiconductor manufacturers from wafer probe through final device validation.

The UltraFLEXplus system has proven to be a key driver in boosting the Semiconductor Test business. In the second quarter of 2026, Teradyne delivered a remarkable 128% year-over-year growth in its Semiconductor Test business, contributing $1.12 billion out of the company's total $1.3 billion in sales. This segment alone accounted for 84% of total sales.

The growing demand for AI-driven applications, particularly in data centers, is expected to continue driving the adoption of UltraFLEXplus. The strong demand for UltraFLEXplus is likely to support top-line growth, strengthening Teradyne's competitive position against KLA and Cohu in the semiconductor test market. For the third quarter of 2026, Teradyne expects revenues in the range of $1.20-$1.30 billion.

How Competitors Fare Against TER

Teradyne is facing stiff competition from companies such as KLA and Cohu. Both companies are expanding their footprint in the AI space.

KLA is benefiting from the growing demand for AI through its leadership in process control and its ability to address growth markets in wafer fab equipment, including high-bandwidth memory and advanced packaging.

In May 2026, Cohu received approximately $5 million in multiple orders for its Diamond X platform from a leading semiconductor manufacturer. The systems will support testing of next-generation GaN power devices for AI data centers, strengthening Cohu's position in AI infrastructure and high-efficiency power semiconductor testing.

AMKR's recent decline appears to be driven primarily by near-term Communications weakness, ongoing smartphone and memory-related pressures, the temporary System-in-Package (SiP) transition and concerns surrounding its heavy capacity investments. However, these challenges need to be viewed against Amkor's broader long-term strategy. The company is increasing investment in advanced packaging, expanding its manufacturing footprint and deepening relationships with key semiconductor players.

Importantly, Amkor's recent investments are increasingly aligned with some of the semiconductor industry's strongest structural growth trends. The company is seeing rising demand for Advanced Packaging, AI and high-performance computing (HPC), automotive and ADAS applications, while its strategic partnerships with TSMC and NVIDIA could strengthen its position.

Therefore, this recent price drop could present an opportunity for investors to buy shares at a lower price and participate in Amkor's long-term growth potential.

Strong Advanced Packaging Growth Supports AMKR

Amkor's long-term growth prospects are increasingly tied to the structural shift toward Advanced Packaging, as rising AI, high-performance computing (HPC) and data-center complexity require higher integration, performance and power efficiency. The company has established capabilities across 2.5D integration, high-density fan-out (HDFO), advanced flip chip, wafer-level processing and advanced SiP. Its second quarter 2026 results showed this opportunity gaining traction, with advanced products generating $1.56 billion of revenue, up from $1.23 billion a year earlier. It also reported growing customer engagements across 2.5D, HDFO and emerging co-packaged optics, including a data-center CPU HDFO program that began ramping in the second quarter.

The opportunity extends beyond near-term revenue growth because advanced packaging can support higher-value applications and improve Amkor's overall product mix and earnings power. The company is deepening strategic relationships with TSMC and NVIDIA, while expanding advanced-packaging capacity in Arizona and Korea. Management said several technology platforms were already operating at full capacity and that customer engagements increasingly involve longer planning horizons and capacity alignment. This is important for investors, as a greater mix of advanced packaging will enable AMKR to capture more value from the growth of AI and HPC, while simultaneously facilitating better utilization of its expanded manufacturing base.

Story Continues

Geographic Diversification Gives AMKR a Competitive Edge

Amkor's broad and strategically located manufacturing footprint is a key competitive advantage, giving customers greater geographic flexibility, supply-chain resiliency and regional manufacturing options. The company's facilities across key regions in Asia and Europe allow customers to diversify supply chains and mitigate operational risks, while its U.S. headquarters and new Arizona facility strengthen its ability to support customers seeking to regionalize semiconductor production. Importantly, AMKR's geographic diversity also allows it to qualify production at multiple sites and optimize asset utilization, providing greater flexibility as customer demand shifts across markets and technologies.

Amkor is expanding this footprint in a way that is increasingly aligned with long-term customer requirements. Phase 1 of the Arizona facility is fully committed, while new capacity is being added in Korea, including a Songdo assembly and test building and additional Gwangju cleanroom capacity expected to support data-center and advanced-packaging opportunities from 2028 onward. Amkor is also expanding facilities in Vietnam, Portugal and Taiwan. The move of SiP production from Korea to Vietnam is particularly strategic because it frees capacity in Korea for rapidly scaling, higher-value Computing programs while increasing SiP and NAND capacity in Vietnam.

Amkor's geographic diversification could become an increasingly important competitive advantage as semiconductor customers seek greater supply-chain resilience and regionalized production. While Micron Technology, Cohu and KLA Corporation also maintain broad global footprints, their geographic networks support different business models. AMKR's footprint is directly aligned with its OSAT operations, enabling customers to access packaging and test capacity across multiple locations. Its investments in Arizona, Korea, Vietnam, Portugal and Taiwan further strengthen this flexibility and align capacity with evolving customer requirements. For investors, this could help AMKR win new programs, deepen customer relationships and support more durable long-term growth.

AMKR Stock Trades Lower Than Its Growth Prospects

Amkor shares appear attractively valued, offering investors a potentially compelling entry point relative to the company's growth outlook. The stock's Zacks Value Score of A indicates an attractive valuation, while its VGM Score of B suggests better returns.

Amkor's earnings outlook further strengthens the investment case. The Zacks Consensus Estimate for 2026 earnings stands at $2.6 per share, implying robust year-over-year growth of 73.3%. This strong expected earnings expansion suggests that the stock's current valuation may not fully reflect its growth potential.

Amkor Technology, Inc. Price and Consensus

Amkor Technology, Inc. price-consensus-chart | Amkor Technology, Inc. Quote

AMKR also trades at a forward P/B ratio of 2.53X, well below the industry and sector averages of 8.72X and 8.87X, respectively. The significant valuation discount, combined with strong projected earnings growth, indicates that AMKR may be trading below levels justified by its underlying growth prospects, presenting potential upside for value-oriented investors.

AMKR's P/B Ratio (TTTM)

Parting Thoughts on AMKR

Amkor's recent pullback provides an attractive entry point for investors seeking to capitalize on the company's strong long-term growth potential. Strong Advanced Packaging demand, AI and HPC opportunities, geographic diversification and strategic partnerships provide solid growth drivers. Combined with attractive valuation and robust earnings expectations, AMKR's growth-driven prospects make the current dip a potential buying opportunity for investors.

news.Title: 外資百億撐腰台股仍翻黑 穎崴亮燈號召千金股、記憶體三雄救火守住4萬7｜Yahoo財經掃描
news.Content:
權值股漲跌分歧，中小型賣壓湧現，台股高檔震盪守住4萬7！今(8)日加權指數開高後一度上漲逾250點、最高觸及47,578.24點，惟追價力道不足，尾盤轉弱，終場下跌220.49點、跌幅0.47%，收在47,105.78點，成交金額8,783.87億元。權王台積電(2330)盤中最高觸及2505元，尾盤爆賣單，漲幅收斂終場僅漲10元、收2470元，漲幅0.41%，成為守住4萬7的重要支柱；電子類股下跌0.70%，金融類股則上漲1.20%，電金權值走勢明顯分歧。

盤面資金流向記憶體，華邦電(2344)大漲4.44%，南亞科(2408)、旺宏(2337)同步走揚，延續AI需求帶動的缺貨與漲價想像；高價股方面也有亮眼表現，股王信驊(5274)盤中最高衝上19,795元，再度叩關「兩萬金」，但終場漲幅收斂至近平盤，前股后穎崴(6515)則強鎖漲停，鴻勁(7769)、旺矽(6223)皆強漲逾5％。反觀被動元件反彈僅一日，國巨*(2327)、華新科(2492)、禾伸堂(3026)集體回檔。緯創(3231)則因GDR定價折讓及股權稀釋疑慮，重挫7%、收在186元；NB概念股華碩(2357)、仁寶(2324)、宏碁(2353)、英業達(2356)同步下跌逾3%。

亞股早盤走勢分歧，尾盤則多數轉弱，日經指數下跌1.70%，韓國綜合指數下跌0.58%，香港恆生指數下跌0.38%，上海綜合指數逆勢小漲0.20%。

📝盤點熱門股：友達、華邦電、聯電

熱門成交股方面，面板股友達(2409)受賣廠、朝輕資產轉型題材帶動，吸引短線資金積極追逐，股價走揚並爆出62.20萬張，登上成交量冠軍；同為面板雙虎的群創(3481)也因面板股成為資金焦點而交易熱絡，但盤中賣壓浮現、股價走弱，成交量居第四。

記憶體股華邦電(2344)受8月營收年增289.43%、連續第9個月創高，以及法人看好DRAM報價與獲利展望激勵，人氣爆棚，拿下成交量第二名；力積電(6770)則延續記憶體與矽電容題材熱度，多空換手頻繁，尾盤股價小幅收低，排名第五。晶圓代工股聯電(2303)前一日受8月營收改寫近4年新高、連續6個月成長激勵攻上漲停，今日漲停行情降溫、調節賣壓湧現，股價明顯回落，成交量位居第三。

📌三大法人買賣超

三大法人今日合計賣超99.87億元，其中，外資逆勢買超132.69億元，成為唯一站在買方的法人；投信賣超47.15億元，自營商自行買賣與避險部位加總則賣超185.40億元。整體來看，外資雖持續回補，但仍不敵投信與自營商調節力道，三大法人最終轉為賣超。

✨本日議題股：金融股

電子權值股攻勢暫歇，資金轉進具防禦色彩的金融族群撐盤，其中玉山金(2884)成為領漲焦點，前8月稅後純益達280.4億元、年增20.32%，改寫歷年同期新高，每股純益1.73元，激勵股價勁揚、終場收45.55元，幾乎收在全日最高點；此外，台新新光金(2887)、華南金(2880)、中信金(2891)等也獲買盤進駐...... 點我看更多

👥台塑四寶8月營收一次看：

台塑四寶8月營收全數較去年同期成長，但月增率呈現「二增二減」。台塑化(6505)以819.05億元居冠，月增9.5%、年增50.3%，受惠國際油價上漲、煉製與銷售量增加，以及外銷油品價差擴大，年增幅為四寶之最；南亞(1303)營收306億元，月增0.1%、年增46.7%，刷新50個月高點...... 點我看更多

🔭重大財經事件展望

周三國際財經焦點，先看美國市場，將進行3年期公債拍賣；歐洲方面，法國將公布7月工業生產，製造業景氣與經濟動能受關注；亞太區方面，韓國將公布8月失業率，日本則發布9月短觀調查；陸港澳方面，中國大陸將公布8月CPI與PPI年增率，市場聚焦內需復甦與通縮壓力，另有中國國際服務貿易交易會、Inclusion外灘大會及中國國際光電博覽會登場。

台灣方面，財政部將公布8月海關進出口數據；另有中華信評2026台灣企業信用焦點研討會及公平會委員會議登場；企業動態方面，法說會可留意亞德客-KY(1590)、光寶科(2301)、瑞昱(2379)、廣達(2382)、中信金(2891)、嘉澤(3533)、臻鼎-KY(4958)及譜瑞-KY(4966)等大廠，營運展望有望牽動盤面資金輪動，另神達(3706)、富喬(1815)同步除權息，填權息行情亦值得觀察。

news.Title: 【Follow法人】外資續加碼132億元！掃貨華邦電南亞科逾12萬張 鴻海廣達6檔「老AI」淪刀下魂
news.Content:
（下午4點35分更新買賣超個股）

台股今（8）日開高走低，終場下跌220.49點，收在47,105.78點。三大法人僅外資持續站在買方「撿便宜」，但加碼力道明顯收斂，買超台股132.69億元，敲進記憶體雙雄華邦電（2344）、南亞科（2408）逾12萬張，反手大砍緯創（3231）、仁寶（2324）、英業達（2356）、宏碁（2353）、廣達（2382）及鴻海（2317）等6檔老AI股，單日合計遭外資賣超逾13萬張。

外資今日買超前三大：華邦電、友達、南亞科

記憶體雙雄成為外資今日掃貨重心，華邦電（2344）獲買超9萬2,597張，高居買超冠軍；南亞科（2408）則獲加碼3萬4,279張，排名第三。兩檔合計吸金12萬6,876張，占買超前十大總張數近4成。

面板雙雄則呈現一買一賣，友達（2409）獲外資大買8萬5,222張，位居買超第二名；群創（3481）卻遭反手賣超4萬2,072張，排名賣超第三。

金融股今日也受外資青睞，共有4檔擠進買超前十大。台企銀（2834）獲買超2萬6,847張，居金融股之首；第一金（2892）、兆豐金（2886）與上海商銀（5876）則分別獲搶進1萬6,065張、1萬3,421張及1萬1,795張，合計買超6萬8,128張。

外資今日賣超前三大：聯電、緯創、群創

反觀「老AI」成為外資提款重災區，晶圓代工二哥聯電（2303）遭調節6萬3,878張，成為外資今日提款最多的個股；緯創（3231）遭賣超4萬6,059張，居賣超第二名；仁寶（2324）、英業達（2356）與宏碁（2353）分別被砍2萬8,275張、1萬8,177張及1萬4,607張。

廣達（2382）及鴻海（2317）也未能逃過賣壓，分別遭外資賣超1萬3,586張、1萬3,289張。若依廣達收盤價328元、鴻海收盤價251.5元粗估，外資分別提款約44.56億元及33.42億元，合計近78億元。

外資獨站買方續加碼132億元 分析師：看好台股

根據證交所公布籌碼動向，三大法人今日合計賣超99.87億元。其中，外資續加碼132.69億元，連3個交易日累計買超達1577.9億元。

投信今日賣超47.15億元，呈現由買轉賣；自營商同樣轉賣，合計賣超185.4億元，其中自行買賣部分賣超28.85億元、避險操作賣超156.55億元。

台股今日開高走低，盤中一度攻上47,578.24點，但追價力道不足，獲利了結與解套賣壓接連出籠，老AI族群成為重災區，指數隨後翻黑，終場下跌220.49點、收47,105.78點，成交金額9,195.5億元。

啟發投顧分析師萬相和表示，本周重要事件及經濟數據密集，包括美債回購細節、美國生產者物價指數（PPI）、消費者物價指數（CPI）陸續公布，市場近期也持續討論升息議題。在不確定因素仍多的情況下，外資今日仍願意加碼台股，顯示對後市保有一定信心，成為觀察盤面的關鍵訊號，預期資金主要鎖定台積電（2330）、聯電（2303）等大型權值股，記憶體族群也可能持續獲得買盤關注；相較之下，中小型股現階段宜提高警覺。

至於投信轉為賣超，萬相和認為，台股今日盤中最高來到47,578點，逐漸逼近6月歷史高點48,218點附近，部分基金先前在高檔建立不少部位，如今指數再度回到相對高檔，投信可能趁勢調節持股，並透過避險操作降低風險，態度相對保守仍屬合理。

馮萱榕／財經特派記者，主跑財政部、電腦通路、觀光餐飲等

news.Title: 記憶體挑大樑！南亞科登吸金王、華邦電逆勢漲逾5% 分析師看多頭未完
news.Content:
台股今（8）日開高走低，一度由紅翻黑，不過記憶體族群逆勢點火，成為盤面撐盤要角。南亞科（2408）早盤大漲逾4%，最高來到538元，開盤不到一小時，成交金額便衝上257億元，居台股之冠；華邦電（2344）也勁揚逾半根停板，最高觸及190.5元，成交金額達246億元，緊追在後。分析師表示，若台股未來要挑戰4萬8、甚至更高的關卡，記憶體不可能缺席，近期族群經歷技術面震盪後迅速止穩，顯示波段行情尚未結束。

台股今日開高後一度衝上47,449.67點、上漲120點，但隨著台積電漲勢收斂、回到平盤附近，電子權值股跟著轉弱，指數隨即翻黑，盤中跌點一度擴大至逾200點。記憶體族群則是逆勢撐盤，截至上午9時50分，華邦電盤中大漲逾5%、最高來到190.5元，重返近兩個月高點，成交量突破13.6萬張，開盤不到一小時便超越昨（7）日全日成交量。

其餘記憶體個股多數維持紅盤，群聯（8299）、威剛（3260）、宇瞻（8271）、創見（2451）、品安（8088）、十銓（4967）、旺宏（2337）、晶豪科則是維持上揚，漲幅落在0.5%至2.5%左右；力積電則是股價震盪走弱。

華冠投顧分析師陳韋廷指出，記憶體是 AI 的必備關鍵元件，若台股未來要挑戰4萬8、甚至更高的關卡，記憶體產業絕不可能缺席。 台廠首要觀察雙雄華邦電與南亞科指標股，因直接生產記憶體顆粒，能更直接受惠於此波行情。

陳韋廷續指，法人目前預估華邦電明年 EPS 可達 63 元，相較目前僅 100 多元的股價，本益比極低。且華邦電不單只有記憶體業務，還與台積電進行更深度的封裝與新技術合作，具有高度自主研發與多元化發展的競爭優勢，並在矽電容領域中占有重要地位。

陳韋廷表示，美光上周五已成功突破下降壓力線，若美光、SK海力士等國際大廠以及費城半導體指數持續向上，將能為台股記憶體板塊帶來強大的助攻力道。在操作策略上，由於記憶體族群剛歷經技術面的大洗盤並迅速止穩，顯示整體波段漲勢尚未結束。因此，只要華邦電與南亞科出現拉回震盪，都可以積極尋找進場買點。

王詩婷／財經特派記者，主跑勞動部、半導體、生技等

news.Title: 台股下跌120點！ 記憶體滾量衝高 華邦電、南亞科、旺宏衝4%

news.Title: 台股翻黑急殺！一度跌近200點 聯電、國巨「一日行情」跌逾2％
news.Content:
（9:18更新）台股翻黑下挫，一度跌近200點，權值股台積電撐盤漲10元至2470元，但台達電翻黑跌近1%，昨日強勢股聯電及國巨跌逾2%。記憶體股逆勢走揚，南亞科及華邦電上漲逾3%。

美國股市周一因勞動節（Labor Day）休市一天，目前韓股勁揚逾1.3%，日股翻紅小漲，台股昨日大漲過後，今（8）日開盤小漲逾百點，約來到47449.67點。

台積電漲10元至2470元。聯發科受輝達宣布斥資35億美元（約1100億台幣）認購海外可轉換公司債（ECB）消息激勵，今日股價走強漲逾1%。

聯發科副董事長暨執行長蔡力行近日重申AI ASIC業務在第四季貢獻超過20億美元營收的看法不變，美系外資也看好此次聯發科與輝達深化合作。

聯電公布8月合併營收250.45億元，月增5.03%、年增30.71%，更寫下近4年新高，同時也是歷史單月營收第3高，激勵昨日股價漲停，今日開盤後轉為下跌逾1 %。

記憶體股走揚，南亞科及華邦電上漲逾2%。

林漢偉分析師表示，今日台股進入高檔量縮橫盤，美股因勞動節休市，國際市場缺乏明確方向。電子權值股以個股表現為主，中小型股雖然題材熱絡，但輪動速度偏快，操作上避免追高。

林漢偉分析師強調，在缺乏美股現貨行情的情況下，今天台股主要還是回歸自身籌碼與題材表現，短線特別留意油價、利率以及外資動向。

台股7日終場大漲775.14點或1.67%，收47326.27點，成交量9399.26億元，外資再度加碼台股883.07億元，創台股歷史第四大買超。三大法人合計買超約1138.65億元。

news.Title: The AI Memory Stock That Could Outshine the Obvious Picks
news.Content:
The AI memory trade has become a hot one. Micron (NASDAQ: MU) and Sandisk (NASDAQ: SNDK) have trounced the S&P 500 this year, but investors who are looking for elevated returns may want to consider a smaller memory pick.

Silicon Motion Technology (NASDAQ: SIMO) may have what it takes to outperform these behemoths in the future, especially if it remains underappreciated relative to its peers.

Missed Nvidia in 2009? This Rare Signal Is Flashing Again. In 2009, a "Double Down" signal flashed for a little-known chipmaker called Nvidia. For the first time in years, that same "Total Conviction" signal is flashing for a company 1/100th the size of Nvidia. Continue »

NAND flash controllers are the backbone of memory

Silicon Motion Technology produces NAND flash controllers that enable NAND flash memory. It's a critical component for various memory chips , which explains why the company counts Micron, Sandisk, and other chipmakers as its top customers.

Each of Silicon Motion Technology's customers has reported exceptional results, with multi-year deals highlighted. Micron CEO Sanjay Mehrotra told investors that the company's strategic customer agreements will "significantly enhance the durability and predictability of [the company's] strong financial performance."

Sandisk also reached multi-year deals that offer meaningful revenue visibility through its fiscal 2030. The company also reported 51% sequential growth in its fiscal 2026 fourth quarter while guiding for 20.4% sequential growth at its midpoint.

These companies' success directly translates into more demand for NAND flash controllers. That demand has contributed to Silicon Motion Technology shares soaring by more than 180% year-to-date.

Fundamentals are enjoying major tailwinds

Silicon Motion Technology's stock gains align with its fundamentals . The company reported 127% year-over-year revenue growth in its second quarter. That included a 32% sequential jump in revenue, which comfortably beat guidance.

Investors were expecting up to $411 million in Q2 revenue based on guidance. However, Silicon Motion Technology actually delivered $451 million. Even better, the CEO said that the company has built a "resilient platform for sustainable, high-quality revenue and profitability growth for years to come."

That commentary implies that Silicon Motion Technology's recent successes aren't a one-off event. Guidance for the third quarter implies up to $541 million in revenue, representing a 20% sequential jump.

Micron and Sandisk both crushed recent guidance, and since they are some of Silicon Motion Technology's largest customers, it increases the likelihood of the latter crushing its Q3 forecast. Silicon Motion Technology will likely report earnings in late October, giving investors time to accumulate before the big day.

Story Continues

To top it all off, the growth stock trades at a price-to-earnings ratio of just 28. The valuation will get more attractive in subsequent quarters as its revenue and net income continue to surge.

news.Title: ASML Bets Big on AI & Capacity Expansion: Should You Buy the Stock?
news.Content:
ASML Holding N.V. ASML is increasingly benefiting from the growing adoption of AI, rapid advances in leading-edge Logic and Memory technologies and the need for sophisticated semiconductor manufacturing processes. The company is one of the biggest beneficiaries of the increasing technology complexity of the semiconductor ecosystem, which is driving demand for its lithography equipment.

AI Boom Fuels Advanced Logic & Memory Demand

Rapid expansion of AI infrastructure is one of ASML's most powerful growth catalysts. Training and inference workloads require increasingly powerful and energy-efficient processors, which are accelerating the transition toward smaller process nodes and more advanced memory technologies.

The ongoing investments and continued progress in AI technologies are further boosting demand for both advanced Logic and Memory chips. Semiconductor manufacturers are accelerating capacity expansion plans, resulting in stronger commitments across ASML's product portfolio.

Growing demand for high-bandwidth memory alongside tighter supplies of conventional DRAM is encouraging memory manufacturers to build additional capacity. At the same time, migration toward advanced DRAM nodes requires greater lithography intensity, benefiting both extreme ultraviolet (EUV) and deep ultraviolet (DUV) immersion demand.

Near-term trends remain equally encouraging. ASML now expects to ship approximately 65 Low-NA EUV systems in 2026, supporting year-over-year EUV net system sales growth of more than 45%. The rising contribution of EUV should also benefit ASML as semiconductor customers continue pushing their technology roadmaps forward to meet the performance and power-efficiency requirements of AI computing.

Image Source: Zacks Investment Research

Capacity Expansion Bodes Well

ASML's decision to materially increase manufacturing capacity provides another indication of strengthening demand visibility. Based on strong customer commitments, the company plans to increase its 2027 Low-NA EUV capacity by approximately 30% from its 2026 capacity of roughly 65 systems. It is also evaluating another approximately 30% capacity increase for 2028.

A similar expansion is underway for immersion DUV. ASML plans to raise capacity by approximately 30% in 2027 from a 2026 level of roughly 130 systems and is evaluating another 30% increase for 2028. These initiatives are particularly encouraging because lithography systems have long production lead times and require close coordination with customers and ASML's extensive supply chain. Capacity expansion therefore suggests that customers are providing ASML with increased visibility into their multi-year fab and technology plans.

The broader semiconductor industry's long-term expansion provides an attractive backdrop for ASML. The increasing semiconductor content required for AI, cloud computing, automotive applications and other digital technologies should support additional wafer capacity and technology investments.

Story Continues

Price Performance

ASML has gained a stellar 115.4% over the past year compared with the sector's growth of 27.7%. It has outperformed peers like Advanced Energy Industries, Inc. AEIS but lagged Silicon Motion Technology Corporation SIMO. While AEIS has gained 81.9%, SIMO has soared 202% over this period.

One-Year ASML Stock Price Performance

Estimate Revision Trend

Earnings estimates for ASML for 2026 have moved up 58.1% to $44.99 over the past year, while the same for 2027 has increased 79.9% to $59.36. The positive estimate revision depicts bullish sentiment about the stock's growth potential.

Elevated Operational Risks Persist

Despite the positives, management attributes the current demand environment primarily to AI-related investment and the resulting need for more advanced Logic and Memory capacity. This has produced unusually long order visibility for ASML, but it also makes the growth profile increasingly dependent on customers maintaining those expansion plans. A slower pace of customer investment would therefore affect both system demand and utilization of the larger production footprint ASML is preparing.

The planned scale-up requires manufacturing capacity, suppliers and trained employees to rise together. This leaves future profitability dependent on converting the larger cost base into the expected shipment volumes. Moreover, a uniform adoption schedule across Logic and DRAM customers is yet to be established. High-NA therefore remains both a technology opportunity and an execution variable, with the pace of wider insertion dependent on customer qualification and manufacturing decisions rather than ASML's roadmap alone.

End Note

ASML appears well positioned to capitalize on multiple semiconductor growth trends. Accelerating AI investments are driving leading-edge Logic and Memory capacity additions, while increasing lithography intensity supports greater demand for EUV and DUV systems. At the same time, ASML's planned production-capacity increases strengthen the growth outlook. Positive estimate revisions remain an additional tailwind.

However, export restrictions, geopolitical tensions and the semiconductor industry's inherently cyclical capital-spending patterns remain factors to monitor. Its growth also depends on customers sustaining elevated capital spending. An additional risk is that ASML expanding output without disrupting costs or supply could dent its growth prospects.

With a Zacks Rank #3 (Hold), ASML appears to be treading in the middle of the road, and new investors could be better off if they trade with caution. You can see the complete list of today's Zacks #1 Rank (Strong Buy) stocks here .

news.Title: Can Silicon Motion's CRA Compliance Efforts Drive Future Growth?
news.Content:
Silicon Motion Technology Corporation SIMO has strengthened its product cybersecurity framework by reaching an initial milestone in its compliance program for the European Union's Cyber Resilience Act (CRA). The milestone underscores the company's strategy to improve product security alongside its expanding presence in artificial intelligence (AI), data center and edge computing markets.

Silicon Motion has aligned its product security controls and internal processes with the CRA's incident-reporting requirements while enhancing its vulnerability-handling capabilities. It has reinforced security management and due diligence for third-party hardware and software components, continuous vulnerability monitoring, coordinated disclosure and remediation, and incident escalation and reporting procedures.

The company has also launched a dedicated security vulnerability reporting channel that allows customers, end users and other stakeholders to report suspected issues directly. This initiative supports the timely identification and resolution of vulnerabilities across its portfolio, including enterprise and edge SSD controllers, enterprise boot drive solutions, embedded eMMC and UFS controllers, Ferri solutions for automotive and Physical AI applications, and display interface products.

As connected devices and AI infrastructure increasingly depend on secure hardware and software, Silicon Motion's focus on product security and post-market vulnerability management could enhance the reliability and competitiveness of its storage solutions.

How Are Competitors Advancing in Cybersecurity?

Silicon Motion faces competition from Micron Technology, Inc. MU and Western Digital Corporation WDC. Micron Technology continues to focus on cybersecurity by integrating security features such as secure boot, hardware root of trust and encryption into its products. The company uses the NIST Cybersecurity Framework to guide its broader cybersecurity programs and risk management. Micron Technology has strengthened security measures for its SSDs and provides channels for reporting potential product security issues.

Western Digital is advancing its cybersecurity efforts by integrating post-quantum cryptography into its Ultrastar hard drives. The technology includes secure boot and firmware protection to help improve device security and protect AI data. Western Digital plans to expand its post-quantum cryptography capabilities across additional enterprise hard drive product lines over time to enhance data protection and hardware security.

Story Continues

SIMO's Price Performance, Valuation and Estimates

Silicon Motion shares have skyrocketed 202% over the past year compared with the industry's growth of 206.8%.

Image Source: Zacks Investment Research

Going by the price/earnings ratio, the company's shares currently trade at 17.42 forward earnings, higher than 11.95 for the industry.

Earnings estimates for 2026 have increased 31.6% to $11.16 over the past 60 days, while those for 2027 have increased 50.3% to $16.34.

Silicon Motion stock currently sports a Zacks Rank #1 (Strong Buy). You can see the complete list of today's Zacks #1 Rank stocks here .

news.Title: ADI Declines 5.6% in a Month: Time to Buy, Sell or Hold the Stock?
news.Content:
Analog Devices ADI shares have lost 5.6% in the past month compared with the Zacks Semiconductor - Analog and Mixed industry's decline of 6.1%.

ADI One Month Performance Chart

Image Source: Zacks Investment Research

ADI is trading at a forward price-to-sales multiple of 9.76X, much above the industry's 7.74x. This premium valuation is further supported by the Zacks Value Score of D.

ADI Forward 12-Month (P/S) Performance Chart

Given the dynamics, investors are wondering if it is the right time to invest in ADI stock. Let's delve deeper into the fundamentals and financials to know if it is the right time to buy, sell or retain ADI stock.

ADI Benefits From Industrial and Data Center Strength

ADI's data center and power businesses are emerging as major growth drivers as AI infrastructure requires significantly higher power density, efficiency and monitoring capabilities. The company is benefiting from the shift toward 800V DC power distribution, driving increasing demand for 800V-to-intermediate power conversion technologies. ADI's acquisition of Empower Semiconductor further strengthens its vertical power capabilities by enabling power delivery closer to the processor package.

Optical connectivity represents another important growth opportunity as AI data centers transition toward higher-speed architectures. ADI supplies timing, power management, data conversion, monitoring and control technologies for optical systems as customers move from 800 gigabits to 3.2 terabits per second. The company expects optical circuit switching revenues to approximately double in fiscal 2026, with similar growth targeted for fiscal 2027.

Co-packaged optics is also expanding ADI's opportunity as rising thermal and serviceability complexity increases the need for precision control technologies. Analog Devices' Industrial segment accounted for 49% of fiscal third-quarter 2026 revenues, rising 53% year over year and 10% sequentially to $1.97 billion. With continued investment, ADI is benefiting from higher revenues, improved utilization, favorable product mix and pricing actions.

ADI's third-quarter adjusted gross margin increased 330 basis points year over year to 72.5%, while adjusted operating margin expanded 780 basis points to 50.0%. Adjusted operating expenses were $906.8 million, or 22.5% of revenue, compared with 27.1% a year earlier. Management expects further margin improvement in the fourth quarter, supported by favorable mix, higher fixed-cost absorption and pricing actions.

Story Continues

ADI Sustains Margins Despite Competitive Pressure

Competition in the high-performance analog semiconductor market remains intense, with Texas Instruments identified as a key rival given its manufacturing scale. ADI retains leadership in converters, although competitors continue to compete across multiple analog categories. ADI competes with Texas Instruments TXN, STMicroelectronics STM and NXP Semiconductors NXPI.

Texas Instruments competes across analog, digital and mixed-signal solutions, including precision sensing and power-management products for consumer electronics. NXP is a major provider of analog and mixed-signal semiconductor solutions for mobile, connectivity and consumer applications, including front-end, power-management and mixed-signal products, particularly in the mobile and IoT markets.

Texas Instruments also targets the automotive market through analog sensors, power ICs, in-vehicle networking, signal-chain products, and driver-assistance electronics. STMicroelectronics competes with ADI through products, including MEMS and inertial sensors, analog front ends, interface ICs and microcontrollers. Competition from these major semiconductor players has prompted ADI to increase research and development and sales and marketing investments at double-digit rates. Strong revenue growth has helped the company maintain its margins.

The Zacks Consensus Estimate for fiscal 2026 earnings is pegged at $12.96 per share, implying 66.4% year-over-year growth. The consensus estimate has also moved higher over the past 30 days.

Conclusion: Buy ADI Stock Now

Analog Devices is benefiting from a broad-based recovery as Industrial demand improves and AI-related data center activity expands across optical and power applications. Long-cycle exposure to automation, test, aerospace and defense, energy systems and vehicle electrification supports durable growth. Sticky design wins and a flexible hybrid manufacturing model help capture demand while keeping channel inventories lean. Based on these factors, we recommend investors consider this Zacks Rank #2 (Buy) stock. You can see the complete list of today's Zacks #1 Rank (Strong Buy) stocks here .

news.Title: Is Microchip Technology Stock Underperforming the S&P 500?
news.Content:
Microchip Technology Incorporated (MCHP) is a global semiconductor company focused on embedded control. The Chandler, Arizona-based company designs, manufactures, and sells microcontrollers, FPGAs, analog, power, connectivity, and timing components and systems for industrial, automotive, consumer, aerospace, defense, communications, and computing markets. The company has a market capitalization of approximately $40.3 billion.

Companies worth between $10 billion and $200 billion are generally classified as "large-cap stocks," and Microchip Technology comfortably fits this category. Its substantial market capitalization reflects its size, influence, and established presence in the semiconductor industry. Microchip benefits from a diverse portfolio of microcontrollers and analog chips serving consumer, automotive, and industrial markets. Its leadership in 8-bit MCUs, expansion into higher-end products, and opportunities in AI, IoT, automation, and connected devices support its long-term growth prospects.

More News from Barchart

Micron Stock More Than Tripled in 2026. Now Taiwan Strike Threat Could Shake the AI Boom.

Amazon Layoffs Continue: How to Play AMZN Stock Now in September 2026

Our exclusive Barchart Brief newsletter is your FREE midday guide to what's moving stocks, sectors, and investor sentiment - delivered right when you need the info most. Subscribe today!

Despite the notable feats, MCHP is currently 30% below its 52-week high of $105.91, reached on May 8, 2026. The stock has also declined 23% over the past three months, significantly underperforming the S&P 500 ($SPX), which has risen 1.8% over the same period.

The stock's 15.1% gain over the past 52 weeks has underperformed the S&P 500's 18.7% return over the same period. However, shares of MCHP have climbed 16.4% year-to-date, outperforming the SPX's 12.8% YTD gain.

MCHP has traded below its 50-day moving average since late June and below its 200-day moving average since late August, suggesting a downward trend.

Microchip Technology lagged the broader market over the past year, potentially reflecting underlying weakness in its financial performance. Over the past five years, the company's revenue declined 2.1% annually, while EPS fell 9.6% and its free cash flow margin dropped 15 percentage points. These trends point to weaker demand and profitability pressures that may have weighed on investor sentiment.

However, MCHP shares jumped about 13.9% on August 7, after the company reported its fiscal Q1 2027 results. Its non-GAAP net income per share of 76 cents surpassed Wall Street's expectations of 70 cents, while net sales of $1.49 billion exceeded forecasts of $1.45 billion.

Story Continues

Within the competitive semiconductor industry, NVIDIA Corporation (NVDA) has demonstrated strong performance and outperformed MCHP, gaining 23.5% year to date and 34.2% over the past 52 weeks.

Nevertheless, Wall Street analysts are bullish on MCHP's prospects. The stock carries a consensus "Strong Buy" rating from the 26 analysts covering it. The mean price target of $109.08 implies 47.1% upside from current levels.

news.Title: 全球記憶體第2季營收增近6成 台廠業績暴衝
news.Content:
受惠於AI伺服器需求爆發以及一般型DRAM（conventional DRAM）合約價顯著上漲，研調機構TrendForce最新調查指出，2026年第二季全球DRAM產業營收達1547.3億美元，季增高達59.5％。其中，三星電子（Samsung）率先出貨HBM4，以39.4％市占率穩坐全球龍頭；台灣記憶體廠南亞科、華邦電與力積電也受惠三大廠製程轉換的外溢效益，單季營收同步繳出亮眼成績。

TrendForce分析，隨著大型語言模型訓練與AI推論刺激需求，HBM3e、LPDDR5X及高容量RDIMM出貨持續攀升，加上原廠庫存處於谷底並優先供貨伺服器，帶動出貨動能。在三大原廠表現上，三星因平均銷售單價拉升，第二季營收季增63.4％達609.8億美元；SK海力士（SK hynix）營收季增37.9％至385.9億美元，市占率24.9％居次；美光（Micron）產品組合轉向高單價產品，營收季增65.5％至360億美元，市占率達23.3％。

台廠方面，在三大原廠將產能推進先進製程之際，成熟製程需求持續湧向台廠。南亞科受惠DDR4與DDR3合約價提高，第二季營收季增68.3％至26.12億美元；華邦電營收季增75.8％至9.98億美元；力積電消費型DRAM營收季增167.8％至1.15億美元，加計代工後季增54％，後續取得美光技術授權後將積極布局產能。

展望第三季，TrendForce指出，雖然位元出貨小幅增長，但因PC與手機客戶對價格負擔能力受限，預估一般型DRAM價格季增幅將收斂至13至18％。

news.Title: 外資上週賣超709億！ 大砍南亞科、華邦電 「這檔」逆勢掃貨8萬張
news.Content:
台股上週維持高檔震盪，外資資金動向卻出現明顯轉折。根據臺灣證券交易所統計，外資在集中市場上週（8月31日至9月4日）總買進金額達2兆1303.28億元，總賣出2兆2013億元，單週賣超709.72億元，終止連續4週買超。台股加權指數9月4日收在4萬6551.13點，單週上漲219.68點、漲幅0.47%。

從外資布局來看，資金明顯轉向金融股。上週外資買超第一名為第一金，達8萬3231張，友達以7萬7581張居次，兆豐金則以7萬6498張排名第3。值得注意的是，買超前10名中竟有8檔金融股，包括台新新光金、合庫金、凱基金、台中銀、華南金及國票金，顯示在台股高檔震盪之際，金融族群成為外資主要加碼標的。

另一方面，電子股則成為外資提款重心。上週賣超冠軍為南亞科，遭外資砍售6萬4235張；華邦電賣超4萬9192張，聯電也遭賣超4萬3201張，前三大賣超標的合計超過15萬張。

不過，市場出現耐人尋味的「外資賣、股價漲」反差。南亞科、華邦電及聯電9月7日股價同步走強，其中聯電更直接攻上漲停，顯示外資前一週的調節並未壓垮市場買盤，反而可能在籌碼換手後迎來反彈行情。

若拉長時間觀察，外資今年以來仍站在大幅賣超的一方。截至9月4日，外資累計賣超集中市場達1兆3898.44億元，持有上市股票市值約72兆5305.75億元，占全體上市股票市值47.99%，單週持有市值減少575.63億元。

（封面圖／東森新聞）
